item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Online Volunteering Program offers people around the world the opportunity to contribute their skills, knowledge, and expertise to global development and humanitarian efforts remotely. Managed by the United Nations Volunteers (UNV) programme, this initiative allows volunteers to support United Nations agencies, governments, public institutions, and civil society organizations online from any location.

Whether you are a student, graduate, young professional, freelancer, or experienced expert, the UN Online Volunteering Program provides a flexible way to gain international experience, support meaningful causes, and contribute to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) without traveling abroad.

Applicants from all countries can participate, and there is no application fee.

Key Summary of the UN Online Volunteering Program

Program Details Information
Host Organization United Nations Volunteers (UNV)
Program Type Online / Virtual Volunteering
Location Fully Remote
Eligible Applicants Open Worldwide
Age Requirement 18 Years and Above
Duration Up to 12 Weeks
Weekly Commitment Up to 20 Hours Per Week
Application Fee None
Certificate Official UN Certificate of Appreciation
Deadline Open Year-Round

What is the UN Online Volunteering Program?

The UN Online Volunteering Program is a global platform that connects volunteers with organizations working in sustainable development, humanitarian action, education, climate action, youth empowerment, gender equality, health, communications, and many other fields.

Through the platform, volunteers can contribute remotely to projects and assignments requiring different skills and expertise. Assignments are available in areas such as:

  • Research and data analysis
  • Graphic design
  • Translation and interpretation
  • Social media management
  • Content writing and editing
  • Communications and advocacy
  • Teaching and training
  • Web development
  • Project support
  • Administrative assistance

The program enables volunteers to collaborate virtually with organizations worldwide while building practical international development experience.

Why Apply for the UN Online Volunteering Program?

The UN Online Volunteering Program is one of the best remote international volunteering opportunities available for students and professionals seeking global exposure and meaningful impact.

1. Gain International Experience

Volunteers work with organizations engaged in development and humanitarian projects around the world. This provides valuable international exposure and practical experience.

2. Build Your CV and Professional Profile

Having United Nations volunteering experience on your CV can strengthen applications for jobs, internships, scholarships, fellowships, and graduate programs.

3. Work Remotely from Anywhere

The program is fully online, allowing participants to volunteer from home without relocation or travel expenses.

4. Receive an Official UN Certificate

Volunteers who successfully complete their assignments receive an electronic certificate of appreciation from the organization they supported.

5. Expand Your Global Network

Participants connect with professionals, organizations, and changemakers from different countries and sectors.

6. Support the Sustainable Development Goals

Volunteers contribute directly to global efforts focused on poverty reduction, education, gender equality, climate action, peacebuilding, and sustainable development.

Eligibility Criteria for the UN Online Volunteering Program 2026

The program is designed to be accessible and inclusive. Applicants from all academic and professional backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

To become an online volunteer, applicants must:

  • Be at least 18 years old
  • Be able to work remotely
  • Have access to the internet and a digital device
  • Demonstrate motivation to support social impact and development initiatives
  • Meet any specific requirements listed for individual assignments

There are no strict academic qualifications required for general participation. Each volunteering assignment may have its own preferred skills or experience.

Duration and Commitment

Online volunteering assignments are flexible and vary depending on the organization’s needs.

Key participation details include:

  • Maximum duration: 12 weeks
  • Maximum workload: 20 hours per week
  • Fully remote collaboration
  • Flexible scheduling depending on the assignment

Organizations can engage up to 25 online volunteers per assignment.

Benefits of the UN Online Volunteering Program

Participants in the program can benefit in several ways:

  • International volunteering experience
  • Practical skill development
  • Exposure to UN-related projects
  • Networking opportunities with global organizations
  • Flexible remote work experience
  • Official recognition certificate
  • Contribution to meaningful social impact initiatives
  • Experience working in multicultural environments

Required Documents

To apply for the UN Online Volunteering Program, applicants generally need:

  • A completed online volunteer profile
  • Personal information and contact details
  • A summary of skills and experience
  • Areas of interest and expertise

Depending on the assignment, organizations may also request:

  • CV or resume
  • Portfolio
  • Writing samples
  • Language certifications
  • Other supporting documents

How the UN Online Volunteering Process Works

The process is straightforward and accessible to applicants worldwide.

Step 1: Organizations Register

Eligible organizations, including UN agencies, NGOs, and public institutions, register on the volunteering platform.

Step 2: Assignments are Published

Organizations submit volunteer assignments outlining the required tasks and skills.

Step 3: Volunteers Apply

Interested volunteers browse available assignments and submit applications for opportunities matching their interests and expertise.

Step 4: Organizations Select Volunteers

Organizations review applications and select suitable candidates.

Step 5: Online Collaboration Begins

Selected volunteers work remotely with the host organization throughout the assignment period.

Step 6: Certificate Issued

Upon successful completion, volunteers receive an official certificate of appreciation.

How to Apply for the UN Online Volunteering Program 2026

Interested applicants can apply online through the official UN Online Volunteering platform.

Application Steps

  1. Visit the official UN Unified Volunteering Platform (UVP).
  2. Create a volunteer profile
  3. Complete your personal and professional information
  4. Browse available assignments
  5. Apply for assignments matching your skills and interests
  6. Wait for the organization’s response
  7. Begin volunteering remotely if selected

Official Website

Applicants can access the official platform here:

UN Online Volunteering Platform

Final Thoughts

The UN Online Volunteering Program 2026 is an excellent opportunity for individuals seeking flexible international experience while contributing to global development efforts. With assignments available year-round and open to applicants worldwide, the program allows volunteers to use their talents to support impactful initiatives from anywhere in the world.

Whether you are looking to build professional experience, strengthen your CV, develop new skills, or contribute to meaningful causes, the UN Online Volunteering Program provides a valuable pathway to engage with global humanitarian and development work remotely.

Looking for more volunteer opportunities worldwide, please visit https://opportunitiesforyouth.org/?s=volunteer

item.content:encoded:
Africa’s innovation ecosystem continues to grow, creating new opportunities for young entrepreneurs, technology enthusiasts, researchers, and aspiring business leaders to develop solutions to the continent’s challenges. However, turning an innovative idea into a successful venture often requires more than creativity. Innovators also need access to experienced professionals who can share practical knowledge, provide guidance, and help them navigate the challenges of developing and growing their ideas.

The timbuktoo Africa UniPods Mentor Network is inviting experienced professionals to contribute to this growing innovation ecosystem by joining its pro bono mentorship network. The initiative seeks to bring together artificial intelligence (AI) and technology experts, industry specialists, and business leaders who can guide innovators across more than 20 African countries.

This opportunity is designed for professionals who want to share their expertise, support emerging innovators, and contribute to the development of Africa’s technology and entrepreneurship ecosystem. By volunteering their knowledge and experience, mentors can help innovators think through challenges, strengthen their ideas, and make progress towards developing solutions with practical value.

Applications are open until 15 November 2026. Interested professionals can apply through the application link provided in the announcement.

About the timbuktoo Africa UniPods Mentor Network

The timbuktoo Africa UniPods Mentor Network is a pan-African mentorship initiative that aims to connect innovators with experienced people who can provide professional guidance and knowledge in relevant fields.

The network brings together individuals with different areas of expertise, including AI, technology, specialised industries, and business leadership. This broad range of experience can help innovators access perspectives that extend beyond technical development and cover the wider process of building, testing, and advancing new ideas.

Innovation often requires collaboration between people with different skills. A technology developer, for example, may have the technical ability to create a product but need advice on identifying customers, understanding market needs, or developing a sustainable business model. Similarly, an entrepreneur with a promising idea may benefit from guidance on using digital technologies, improving operations, or identifying opportunities for growth.

A mentor network can help bridge these knowledge gaps by connecting innovators with professionals who have experience in relevant areas.

Through this initiative, timbuktoo Africa is seeking to build a community of mentors who can contribute to the growth of innovators across more than 20 African countries. The pan-African approach creates an opportunity for expertise to support innovation beyond individual organisations, industries, and national borders.

What Is the Purpose of the Mentor Network?

The main purpose of the UniPods Mentor Network is to make professional knowledge and experience available to Africa’s next generation of innovators.

Innovators frequently encounter challenges that require guidance from people who have already worked in their chosen fields. These challenges may involve technical decisions, product development, business strategy, customer needs, or the practical steps required to move an idea forward.

By bringing experienced professionals into a shared mentorship network, the initiative aims to connect innovators with people who can help them approach such challenges more effectively.

The programme’s stated focus on AI and technology experts, domain specialists, and business leaders also recognises that innovation is not limited to one discipline. Successful solutions may require a combination of technical knowledge, an understanding of a particular industry, and the ability to turn an idea into a viable venture.

The network therefore offers a way for professionals to contribute their expertise to a wider community of innovators working across Africa.

Who Is timbuktoo Africa Looking For?

According to the announcement, timbuktoo Africa is looking for mentors with expertise in three broad areas: artificial intelligence and technology, specialised professional fields, and business leadership.

1. Artificial Intelligence and Technology Experts

Professionals working in AI and technology are among the intended participants in the mentor network.

Artificial intelligence, software development, digital platforms, and other emerging technologies are increasingly relevant to the development of new products and services. Innovators working in these areas may need guidance on technical approaches, the practical application of technology, and the challenges associated with developing solutions for real-world use.

AI and technology professionals who have relevant knowledge and experience may be able to contribute by helping innovators better understand technical possibilities, evaluate approaches, and navigate challenges within their fields.

Potential areas of relevant expertise may include software development, data science, AI applications, digital product development, and other technology-related disciplines. However, the announcement does not provide a formal list of accepted technical specialisations, so applicants should confirm the requirements through the official application form.

2. Domain Specialists

Domain specialists are professionals with substantial knowledge of a particular industry, discipline, or area of practice.

Their experience can help innovators understand the environments in which their ideas may be applied. An innovator developing a solution for a specific sector, for example, may need to understand industry practices, user requirements, operational challenges, and the factors that influence whether a proposed solution will work in practice.

Domain specialists can provide context that may not be readily available through technical research alone. Their professional insights can help innovators assess the relevance of their ideas and consider the practical challenges associated with implementing them.

The announcement does not identify a fixed list of industries or specialist disciplines. Professionals should therefore review the application form to establish whether their particular field of expertise matches the network’s current needs.

3. Business Leaders

Business leaders are another key group invited to contribute to the UniPods Mentor Network.

Developing an innovative product or service is only one part of building a successful venture. Innovators may also need to understand customers, assess market opportunities, organise resources, establish partnerships, and make decisions about growth.

Experienced business leaders can offer practical perspectives on these challenges, drawing on their professional knowledge and experience.

Their contribution may be particularly relevant to innovators who need guidance on the commercial or organisational aspects of developing their ideas. Business experience can also help innovators consider how their solutions could respond to actual needs and operate within the markets they intend to serve.

The announcement does not specify a minimum number of years of business experience or require a particular executive title. Applicants should check the official application form for any additional criteria.

Why Join the timbuktoo Africa UniPods Mentor Network?

Joining the network offers professionals an opportunity to contribute to Africa’s innovation ecosystem by sharing knowledge and experience with emerging innovators.

The announcement specifically presents the network as a pro bono mentorship opportunity. This means prospective mentors should understand that the role is intended as a voluntary professional contribution rather than a paid employment position.

Several reasons may make the opportunity attractive to experienced professionals.

Contribute to Africa’s Innovation Ecosystem

Professionals can use their knowledge to support innovators who are developing ideas, products, technologies, or business solutions.

Mentorship provides a way to contribute beyond one’s immediate workplace or professional network. By helping emerging innovators think through challenges, experienced professionals can play a part in strengthening the wider environment in which innovation takes place.

Share Practical Knowledge and Experience

Professional expertise often develops through years of solving problems, making decisions, and learning from successes and setbacks.

Sharing that experience can help innovators gain a better understanding of the issues they may face. Rather than relying only on theory, innovators can learn from practical perspectives relevant to their work.

The network’s focus on specialists from different professional backgrounds may also allow mentors to contribute knowledge that is directly connected to their areas of competence.

Support Innovators Across African Countries

The announcement states that the network will guide innovators across more than 20 African countries.

This pan-African reach gives the initiative a regional focus and highlights the importance of connecting expertise with innovation communities in different national contexts.

For mentors, participating in such a network may provide an opportunity to contribute to work that extends beyond a single organisation or country. The precise countries covered, the structure of mentor assignments, and the method of matching mentors with innovators are not specified in the announcement.

Contribute on a Pro Bono Basis

The network is specifically seeking people willing to volunteer their expertise.

This can suit professionals who want to make a contribution through knowledge-sharing and mentorship without treating the opportunity as a conventional paid consultancy or employment arrangement.

Before applying, prospective mentors should ensure they understand the expected commitment, the format of mentorship, and any responsibilities associated with participation.

Connect Expertise with Emerging Ideas

Innovation can benefit when technical specialists, industry professionals, and business leaders share their perspectives with people developing new solutions.

The UniPods Mentor Network seeks to bring these different forms of expertise together. For mentors, this represents an opportunity to direct their professional knowledge towards supporting innovators as they work to advance their ideas.

These are potential benefits of participating in a mentorship network, rather than guaranteed outcomes. The original announcement does not specify particular networking benefits, certificates, financial rewards, or other formal incentives.

What Does Pro Bono Mentorship Mean?

Because timbuktoo Africa explicitly describes the network as pro bono, prospective applicants should understand what this means before submitting an application.

Pro bono work involves providing professional services or expertise voluntarily, without charging the recipient a professional fee for that contribution.

In a mentorship setting, this generally means offering guidance, sharing knowledge, discussing challenges, and helping participants think through decisions relevant to their work.

The precise responsibilities of mentors in the UniPods network have not been detailed in the announcement. It does not state how many hours mentors must contribute, whether sessions will take place online or in person, how long a mentoring relationship will last, or whether mentors will be assigned to individual innovators or groups.

Interested professionals should confirm these details through the application process so they can assess whether the commitment fits their professional schedules and capabilities.

Who Can Apply for the UniPods Mentor Network?

The announcement invites AI and technology experts, domain specialists, and business leaders to join the network.

This indicates that the opportunity is aimed primarily at people who can contribute relevant professional expertise to support innovators.

Applicants should consider the following points when assessing their suitability:

  • Relevant professional knowledge: Your background should align with at least one of the broad areas identified in the announcement, such as AI, technology, a specialised industry, or business leadership.
  • Expertise you can share: You should be able to identify knowledge, practical experience, or professional perspectives that could help innovators address challenges in their work.
  • Willingness to volunteer: The network is described as pro bono, so applicants should be prepared to contribute their expertise on a voluntary basis, subject to the programme’s confirmed terms.
  • Interest in supporting innovators: The initiative is intended to guide Africa’s next generation of innovators, making an interest in knowledge-sharing and professional guidance relevant to the opportunity.

These points reflect the nature and stated purpose of the network, not a complete set of formal eligibility requirements. The announcement does not specify a minimum age, academic qualification, professional certification, number of years of experience, or a mandatory employment status.

It also does not provide a detailed list of eligible nationalities. Although the network is pan-African and is intended to support innovators across more than 20 African countries, applicants should not assume that a specific nationality or country of residence is required or excluded without checking the official application form.

How to Apply for the timbuktoo Africa UniPods Mentor Network

Professionals interested in joining the network should begin by accessing the application link shared by timbuktoo Africa.

Application link: https://lnkd.in/dSFp_VDN

Applicants can follow these steps to get started:

  1. Open the official application link. Use the link provided in the timbuktoo Africa announcement to access the application page.
  2. Review the programme information. Read the available details carefully to understand the network’s objectives, the application requirements, and any conditions associated with volunteering as a mentor.
  3. Identify your area of expertise. Consider whether your strongest contribution would be in AI, technology, a specialised professional field, or business leadership.
  4. Prepare an accurate professional profile. Be ready to describe your relevant experience, specialist knowledge, and the areas in which you could provide guidance. Use factual information about your background and capabilities.
  5. Complete the application form. Provide the information requested by the programme and follow any instructions included on the official application page.
  6. Submit before the deadline. The announcement gives 15 November 2026 as the application deadline. Applicants should allow enough time to complete the process and check whether the form includes any additional submission requirements.

The original announcement does not specify the documents required, whether references are necessary, or whether applicants will undergo interviews or another selection stage. Any such requirements should be confirmed through the official application page.

Application Deadline: 15 November 2026

The deadline to apply for the timbuktoo Africa UniPods Mentor Network is 15 November 2026.

Professionals who are interested in sharing their knowledge with emerging African innovators should review the application requirements and submit their applications before the stated closing date.

Because the announcement does not specify the closing time or time zone, applicants should check the application page for any additional deadline instructions rather than assuming that submissions will remain open until a particular hour.

Important Information to Confirm Before Applying

Although the announcement clearly identifies the intended mentor groups, the pan-African scope of the network, its pro bono nature, and the application deadline, several practical details have not been provided.

Before committing to participate, prospective mentors should use the official application process to clarify:

  • The minimum professional experience or qualifications, if any, required.
  • The countries and nationalities eligible to apply.
  • The expected duration of mentorship and the time commitment.
  • Whether mentorship will be delivered online, in person, or through a combination of formats.
  • How mentors will be matched with innovators.
  • Whether there are specific technology fields, industries, or business disciplines currently prioritised.
  • Whether mentors receive formal recognition or other non-financial benefits.
  • The selection process and the anticipated timeline for communicating results.

Confirming these details can help applicants make an informed decision about their suitability and availability.

For more opportunities visit OFY website:https://opportunitiesforyouth.org/?s=jobs

Conclusion

The timbuktoo Africa UniPods Mentor Network offers experienced professionals an opportunity to contribute to the development of Africa’s innovation ecosystem by sharing their knowledge with emerging innovators.

By bringing together AI and technology experts, domain specialists, and business leaders, the initiative aims to connect professional expertise with innovators across more than 20 African countries. Its pro bono approach makes it particularly relevant to people who are willing to volunteer their skills and experience in support of new ideas and developing ventures.

Professionals with relevant expertise and an interest in mentoring are encouraged to review the official application details, assess the expected commitment, and apply if the opportunity aligns with their experience and availability.

Application deadline: 15 November 2026.

Apply here: https://lnkd.in/dSFp_VDN

If you have professional knowledge that could help Africa’s next generation of innovators move their ideas forward, the UniPods Mentor Network is an opportunity to explore how you can contribute.

item.content:encoded:
Overview of the UNICEF Regional Youth Engagement Specialist Opportunity

The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), in partnership with the United Nations Volunteers (UNV) programme, is recruiting an international volunteer for the position of Regional Youth Engagement Specialist in Panama City, Panama. This full-time, onsite assignment offers an opportunity for an experienced professional to support adolescent participation, youth advocacy, strategic communication and programme coordination across Latin America and the Caribbean.

The assignment is advertised as a 12-month placement, with the possibility of extension. The expected start date is 16 November 2026, and the role is based at UNICEF’s regional office in Panama City. The recruitment is competitive, with one assignment available. Candidates should review the eligibility criteria carefully, especially the substantial professional experience requirements and the requirement for fluent Spanish.

Key Opportunity Details

  • Position: Regional Youth Engagement Specialist
  • Host organisation: UNICEF
  • Volunteer programme: United Nations Volunteers (UNV)
  • Duty station: Panama City, Panama
  • Assignment modality: Onsite, on UN premises
  • Volunteer category: International Specialist UCoS from April 2026
  • Duration: 12 months, with possible extension
  • Expected start date: 16 November 2026
  • Work schedule: Full-time
  • Number of vacancies: One
  • Recruitment method: Competitive recruitment
  • Sustainable Development Goal: SDG 17 — Partnerships for the Goals
  • Advertisement deadline: 30 October 2026 at 00:00, as displayed on the UNV listing

Applicants should confirm the deadline and all application instructions directly on the official UN Volunteers platform before submitting an application, as displayed dates and times may depend on the platform’s time zone.

About UNICEF and the Assignment Context

UNICEF works to protect children’s rights, support their survival and development, and help children reach their full potential. Its work spans countries and territories around the world, with particular attention to children and young people who face disadvantage, exclusion or heightened vulnerability.

The assignment supports UNICEF’s commitment to adolescent wellbeing, development and participation as reflected in the Convention on the Rights of the Child, international treaties and decisions of UN intergovernmental bodies. UNICEF seeks to involve adolescents and young people meaningfully and safely in advocacy, policy, programming and humanitarian action, helping accelerate progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals.

In Latin America and the Caribbean, UNICEF operates through its Regional Office (LACRO), based in Panama, and country offices serving 36 countries and territories. The volunteer will support the Advocacy and Communication team, with a particular focus on the positive development and wellbeing of adolescents and young people, including girls’ empowerment, participation and leadership.

The role centres on three broad priorities: establishing and supporting a new cohort of the Regional UNICEF Adolescent Action Board; enabling adolescents and young people to participate in advocacy and communication; and planning, monitoring and supporting youth engagement initiatives across the regional and country offices.

Main Responsibilities and Duties

1. Coordinate the Regional UNICEF Adolescent Action Board

The volunteer will help establish and support a new cohort of the Regional UNICEF Adolescent Action Board (AAB). The aim is to create a functioning, collaborative structure in which adolescents can contribute to UNICEF priorities and shape the work that affects them.

  • Coordinate the board’s selection and orientation process using established criteria.
  • Work with board members to develop a shared workplan and support its implementation, ensuring members’ voices influence the board’s composition and priorities.
  • Design and apply methods that build a sense of community, peer support, collaboration and mentorship among members.
  • Manage a real-time virtual community using tools such as WhatsApp, Microsoft Teams, Zoom and other suitable digital platforms.
  • Apply UNICEF safeguarding protocols to support meaningful and safe participation.
  • Coordinate regular meetings with board members and liaise with UNICEF teams to advance the action plan.
  • Document the board’s establishment and development, and produce members’ interest stories and other communication materials.

2. Support Youth Participation in Advocacy and Communication

The volunteer will help adolescents and young people participate in advocacy and communication activities, including content production, capacity building and engagement in regional events. This includes making participation accessible, organised and safe.

  • Support the production of youth-focused content in different multimedia formats.
  • Facilitate young people’s participation in key regional events, including through training and capacity-building sessions.
  • Coordinate logistics and administrative arrangements for in-person participation, including travel, safeguarding measures, adolescent-friendly materials and orientation sessions.
  • Support adolescent programming and collaboration on regional priorities, including initiatives focused on adolescent girls where relevant.
  • Help co-create initiatives with young people and support innovation aligned with UNICEF programmes and key events.
  • Contribute to funding proposals connected with regional events, UNICEF’s global priority on adolescent girls, and the priorities of adolescents and young people.

3. Plan, Monitor and Support Youth Engagement Across Offices

The assignment includes strategic planning and implementation support for youth engagement at both regional-office and country-office levels. The volunteer will help ensure that engagement activities have clear objectives, credible approaches and measurable results.

  • Contribute to a youth engagement strategy with SMART outcomes, compelling calls to action and a clear theory of change.
  • Analyse relevant political, economic and cultural trends; conduct audience analysis when appropriate; and identify opportunities and challenges.
  • Propose innovative approaches to strengthen the strategy and its implementation.
  • Develop and implement regional communication plans that support youth engagement strategies and mobilise young people around children’s rights and wellbeing.
  • Support country offices in developing youth engagement plans for advocacy and communication.
  • Support a local Youth Advocates programme, including identifying potential advocates, developing their workplans and communication plans, and liaising with UNICEF headquarters in New York.
  • Help youth advocates prepare for events and media opportunities, and document lessons learned and successes.

4. Annual Reporting, Analysis and Quality Assurance

The volunteer will also contribute to results monitoring, reporting and quality assurance. This work helps the regional team understand progress, assess campaign performance and prepare accurate reports.

  • Support regional quality assurance and technical review of country-office annual reports (COARs), results reports in the RAM platform and indicator reporting.
  • Extract and consolidate relevant information for analysis by the regional team.
  • Support preparation of the Regional Office Annual Report (ROAR).
  • Establish baselines against which results can be monitored regularly.
  • Coordinate with monitoring specialists to identify campaign key performance indicators (KPIs) and establish tracking systems.
  • Prepare campaign reports, including milestone, progress and final reports, in collaboration with relevant teams, divisions and partners.

Eligibility Criteria

This is an international assignment and applicants must satisfy the nationality, education, language and experience conditions stated in the vacancy.

  • Age: 18–80 years.
  • Nationality: Candidates must be nationals of a country other than Panama, the country of assignment.
  • Required experience field on the listing: 3 years; the detailed assignment requirements specify at least 5 years of experience in international development and at least 3 years working with adolescents and young people.
  • Education: A bachelor’s degree in international development, social sciences, psychology, communication, education or a related field. A master’s degree is highly preferred.
  • Spanish: Fluent — required.
  • English: Fluent — listed as desirable.
  • French: Working knowledge — desirable.
  • Portuguese: Working knowledge — desirable.

Because Spanish fluency is explicitly required, candidates should not assume that English alone will meet the language requirements. The vacancy also contains both a general experience field and more detailed experience requirements; applicants should use the more specific requirements when assessing their suitability.

Required Skills, Experience and Professional Competencies

Professional experience and technical skills

  • At least five years of experience in international development, including demonstrated project management experience.
  • At least three years of experience working with adolescents and young people in both virtual and in-person settings.
  • Strong understanding of child safeguarding and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) principles, supported by high standards of ethics and integrity.
  • Excellent oral and written communication, drafting, formulation and organisational skills, including experience creating guides and documents for young audiences.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and cultural sensitivity, with the ability to work inclusively and collaboratively with diverse partners and multicultural teams.
  • Self-motivation, sound organisation, the ability to work with limited supervision and the ability to meet tight deadlines.
  • Digital literacy and proficiency with Microsoft Office applications such as Excel, Word, PowerPoint and Teams, as well as the ability to learn new tools quickly.
  • Experience with social media, virtual collaboration platforms and emerging technologies for youth engagement and improved work processes.
  • Demonstrated experience in project design and management, monitoring and evaluation, and results tracking.
  • Experience leading youth engagement strategies, advocacy and communication initiatives, stakeholder networks or coalitions is an asset.

Values and Competencies

  • Care, respect, integrity, trust and accountability.
  • Ability to build and maintain partnerships.
  • Self-awareness and ethical awareness.
  • Commitment to achieving results and impact.
  • Ability to manage ambiguity and complexity.
  • Collaborative working style and respect for different perspectives.

What Makes This Assignment Important?

The position is designed to strengthen the participation of adolescents and young people in the decisions, programmes and public communication that affect their lives. By supporting the Adolescent Action Board, youth advocates, regional campaigns and country-office strategies, the volunteer can help create channels through which young people contribute ideas, share experiences and take part in advocacy.

The role combines communication, programme coordination, youth participation, partnership development, strategy and monitoring. It may be particularly relevant to professionals who have already worked in international development or youth programming and who can demonstrate that they have helped plan projects, coordinate partners, communicate with young audiences and track results.

Duty Station and Living Conditions in Panama City

Panama is located in Central America and has a population of approximately 4.3 million, according to the assignment information. Spanish is the official language. The listing notes that some Panamanians are bilingual and describes Panama City as generally safe, while advising residents to take care in certain areas and protect their personal belongings.

The following practical details are included in the assignment description:

  • Housing: Both houses and apartments are available. The listing notes that some staff choose apartments for the additional security and facilities they may offer.
  • Currency: The US dollar is used as legal currency. Panama also issues Balboa coins of similar value to US dollars; the listing advises leaving the country with US dollars because Balboa currency may be difficult to exchange internationally.
  • Climate: The climate is tropical, with an average temperature of about 27°C year-round and high humidity of approximately 78%. The listed rainy season runs from March through November, so an umbrella may be useful.
  • Office and indoor temperatures: Air conditioning in offices and shops may feel cool, so a light jacket or sweater may be helpful.
  • Electricity: The standard supply is listed as 110 volts, 60 cycles, with two- and three-prong plugs. Some properties may have 220-volt outlets for air conditioning or similar equipment. Power fluctuations and outages can occur.

item.content:encoded:
Young people aged 15 to 24 who are currently residing in Malaysia are invited to participate in a UNICEF Malaysia initiative focused on creating a Manifesto for a Safe, Clean, Healthy and Sustainable Environment. The open call seeks youth leaders who can contribute their perspectives, ideas and experiences to the development of a youth-focused environmental manifesto that will be presented to Members of Parliament.

The initiative provides an opportunity for eligible young people to contribute to discussions about environmental conditions and sustainability, bringing youth voices into conversations with parliamentary representatives. By participating in the co-creation process, selected youth leaders can help articulate young people’s perspectives on the importance of living in a safe, clean, healthy and sustainable environment.

The call is specifically directed at young people aged 15 to 24 who reside in Malaysia. Applicants must also be in Malaysia and available to participate on 14 November, 1 December and 2 December 2026. These dates are essential participation requirements, so interested applicants should check their availability before submitting the form.

The application form collects personal and contact information, details about applicants’ residence, Indigenous identity, accessibility or reasonable accommodation needs, and parental or guardian consent for applicants under 18. Applicants should provide accurate information and review the form carefully before submitting their responses.

1. Overview of the UNICEF Malaysia Youth Environmental Manifesto Call

The open call is associated with UNICEF Malaysia and focuses on youth participation in the development of a manifesto addressing a safe, clean, healthy and sustainable environment.

Key details include:

  • Organiser: UNICEF Malaysia.
  • Opportunity: Youth participation in co-creating an environmental manifesto.
  • Main focus: A Safe, Clean, Healthy and Sustainable Environment.
  • Target participants: Youth leaders aged 15 to 24.
  • Location requirement: Applicants must reside in Malaysia and be in the country for the required programme dates.
  • Required availability: 14 November, 1 December and 2 December 2026.
  • Main activity: Collaboratively developing a manifesto and presenting it to Members of Parliament.
  • Application method: Online application form.
  • Application deadline: Not specified in the supplied announcement and form excerpt.

Applicants should rely on the official application form or communications from UNICEF Malaysia for any additional details, including the submission deadline, selection process and further participation requirements.

2. About UNICEF Malaysia

The United Nations Children’s Fund, commonly known as UNICEF, works to advance the rights and well-being of children. UNICEF Malaysia is the organisation identified in this open call as seeking youth leaders to help develop the environmental manifesto.

The initiative is framed around the participation of young people in expressing their views on environmental issues and presenting a shared manifesto to Members of Parliament. It provides a structured opportunity for eligible youth to contribute to a collective statement concerning the environment in which people live, grow and participate in their communities.

The supplied announcement does not provide further information about the programme’s funding, duration beyond the specified dates, venue, number of selected participants or whether travel and accommodation will be provided. Applicants should seek clarification from the organisers if these details are important to their participation.

3. What Is the Manifesto for a Safe, Clean, Healthy and Sustainable Environment?

A manifesto is a document that presents a set of ideas, priorities, concerns or proposals around a particular issue. In this initiative, the intended manifesto concerns the creation and protection of a safe, clean, healthy and sustainable environment.

UNICEF Malaysia is inviting young people to co-create the manifesto. This means the initiative is intended to involve youth participants in developing its content rather than simply asking them to receive a document prepared by others.

The environmental focus brings together four central ideas:

A. A Safe Environment

The call highlights the importance of a safe environment. The supplied announcement does not define specific safety issues or list particular proposals that the manifesto must address. Applicants can use the application process to learn more about the programme’s intended scope and the topics that participants will discuss.

B. A Clean Environment

Cleanliness is another central element of the proposed manifesto. The initiative’s title identifies a clean environment as one of the outcomes around which youth perspectives will be brought together.

The announcement does not specify whether participants will focus on waste management, pollution, sanitation or other particular issues. Applicants should not assume that any one topic is mandatory unless the organisers provide additional guidance.

C. A Healthy Environment

The call also focuses on a healthy environment. It invites youth leaders to contribute to a manifesto that brings attention to this broad environmental objective.

The supplied information does not provide a detailed health framework or a list of environmental health priorities. The exact issues to be discussed should be confirmed through official programme communications.

D. A Sustainable Environment

Sustainability is the fourth element of the manifesto’s title. The initiative seeks to bring young people’s voices into the development of a shared document on a safe, clean, healthy and sustainable environment.

The announcement does not identify specific sustainability targets, policy recommendations or environmental indicators. These should not be treated as confirmed programme requirements unless they appear in the official materials.

4. Why Youth Participation Is Central to This Initiative

The call specifically seeks youth leaders aged 15 to 24. Its main activity is the collaborative development of a manifesto that will be presented to Members of Parliament.

This makes youth participation a defining feature of the opportunity. Young people who are selected will have the opportunity to contribute their perspectives to a document intended for presentation to parliamentary representatives.

The opportunity may be relevant to young people interested in environmental issues, youth leadership, public participation or advocacy. However, the supplied form does not list environmental qualifications, previous advocacy experience or formal leadership credentials as mandatory admission requirements. Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that a particular qualification or previous project is required unless the full application form states otherwise.

Participation is subject to eligibility, selection and the ability to attend the specified dates. The announcement does not guarantee that every applicant will be selected or that participation will lead to any particular policy outcome.

5. What Selected Participants Are Expected to Do

The announcement identifies two principal activities:

  1. Co-create the environmental manifesto. Youth leaders will contribute to the development of a manifesto centred on a safe, clean, healthy and sustainable environment.
  2. Present the manifesto to Members of Parliament. The initiative includes presenting the completed manifesto to parliamentary representatives.

Applicants must be available on 14 November, 1 December and 2 December 2026 and must be in Malaysia for the programme requirements.

The supplied material does not explain the precise agenda for each date, the expected working hours, the venue or whether all activities will be conducted in person. It also does not provide a detailed description of preparatory work, group assignments, presentation format or follow-up activities. Candidates should confirm these arrangements with UNICEF Malaysia before making travel or scheduling commitments.

6. Eligibility Requirements for Applicants

The announcement establishes several essential participation conditions.

A. Age Requirement

Applicants must be between 15 and 24 years old.

Young people outside this age range are not included in the stated target group. Applicants should provide their correct date of birth in the application form.

B. Residence in Malaysia

The opportunity is intended for youth leaders residing in Malaysia. The form asks applicants to identify both their state or federal territory of origin and their current state or federal territory of residence.

The listed locations are:

  • Johor
  • Kedah
  • Kelantan
  • Melaka
  • Negeri Sembilan
  • Pahang
  • Penang
  • Perak
  • Perlis
  • Sabah
  • Sarawak
  • Selangor
  • Terengganu
  • Labuan
  • Kuala Lumpur
  • Putrajaya

Applicants should select the location that accurately reflects their current residence and separately provide their state or federal territory of origin.

The form’s list identifies Malaysian states and federal territories. It does not provide a separate list of eligible nationalities or explicitly explain whether non-Malaysian citizens who reside in Malaysia may apply. Prospective applicants who are unsure whether their residency status qualifies should seek clarification from UNICEF Malaysia.

C. Availability on the Required Dates

Participants must be available on all three dates specified in the announcement:

  • 14 November 2026.
  • 1 December 2026.
  • 2 December 2026.

Applicants should review their school, university, work and personal commitments before applying. The announcement presents these dates as a participation requirement, so applicants should not assume that missing one date will be permitted.

D. Parental or Guardian Consent for Applicants Under 18

The application form asks applicants under the age of 18 whether they will be able to obtain written consent from a parent or guardian if selected.

Applicants under 18 should be prepared to secure the required written consent if they are chosen to participate. The form offers three responses: Yes, No or Not applicable.

The question is specifically relevant to applicants who are under 18. Applicants aged 18 or older can select the response that corresponds to the form’s instructions.

E. Indigenous Identity

The form asks whether applicants identify as Indigenous. Applicants can answer Yes or No.

The question appears in the personal details section of the application form. The supplied material does not state that Indigenous identity is a condition of eligibility or that only Indigenous applicants may apply. Applicants should answer the question truthfully and should not interpret it as a restriction unless UNICEF Malaysia provides additional guidance.

F. Reasonable Accommodation and Support

Applicants are asked whether they require any reasonable accommodation or support to participate fully in the programme.

If an applicant answers Yes, the form provides a follow-up question asking them to describe the support or accommodation that would help them participate fully.

This gives applicants a way to communicate relevant access or participation needs. Applicants who require support should describe their needs clearly in the designated section. The supplied announcement does not specify which accommodations are available or whether all requests can be provided, so applicants may need to confirm arrangements with the organisers.

7. Information Required in the Application Form

The supplied application form begins with a personal details section. It includes the following questions.

1. Full Name

Applicants must enter their full name. They should use accurate personal details and ensure that their name is entered consistently with relevant identification documents where applicable.

2. Preferred Name

Applicants can provide the name they prefer to be addressed by during the programme.

3. Date of Birth

The form requests the applicant’s date of birth and displays a date-entry format of month/day/year. Applicants should enter the correct date because age is one of the main eligibility requirements.

4. State or Federal Territory of Origin

Applicants select their state or federal territory of origin from the list provided in the form.

5. Current State or Federal Territory of Residence

Applicants identify where they currently reside in Malaysia. This is distinct from their state or federal territory of origin.

6. Email Address

A valid email address is requested so that the applicant can provide contact details. Applicants should use an email account they can access and check regularly.

7. WhatsApp Contact Number

The form requests a WhatsApp contact number. Applicants should enter a correct number and ensure they can receive communications through that channel.

8. Indigenous Identity

Applicants are asked whether they identify as an Indigenous person, with Yes and No options.

9. Reasonable Accommodation or Support

Applicants indicate whether they require reasonable accommodation or support to participate fully.

10. Details of Requested Support

Applicants who answer Yes to the accommodation question can explain what support would help them participate. This question is conditional on the response to the previous question.

11. Written Parental or Guardian Consent for Applicants Under 18

Applicants under 18 are asked whether they can obtain written consent from a parent or guardian if selected. The available responses are Yes, No and Not applicable.

The form also states that personal details such as names and email addresses are not automatically collected unless applicants provide them. It is hosted through Microsoft Forms, and the notice explains that information submitted through the form is sent to the form owner.

The form’s notice also says that the owner has not provided a privacy statement explaining how submitted personal information will be used. Applicants should therefore read the information displayed on the form carefully and contact the organisers if they need clarification about data handling before submitting personal details.

8. How to Apply for the UNICEF Malaysia Youth Environmental Manifesto Call

The supplied material includes the opening page of the application form but does not include a complete public application URL. The form appears to continue across three pages, and the excerpt provided contains the first page.

Interested young people should locate the official UNICEF Malaysia announcement or application form before submitting their details. Once they have accessed the correct form, they should follow the instructions shown on each page.

A practical application preparation process is as follows:

  1. Confirm that you meet the age requirement. Ensure that you are between 15 and 24 years old.
  2. Confirm your residence. Make sure you currently reside in Malaysia and can meet the programme’s location requirements.
  3. Check your availability. Ensure that you can participate on 14 November, 1 December and 2 December 2026.
  4. Prepare your personal information. Have your full name, preferred name, date of birth and residence details ready.
  5. Provide valid contact information. Enter an accessible email address and the correct WhatsApp number.
  6. Answer the Indigenous identity question accurately. Select the response that reflects your circumstances.
  7. Consider any support needs. If you require reasonable accommodation, explain what would help you participate fully.
  8. Arrange parental or guardian consent if applicable. If you are under 18, determine whether you can obtain written consent if selected.
  9. Complete all pages of the form. The supplied excerpt shows page one of three, so applicants should check the remaining pages for additional questions or instructions.
  10. Review your responses before submitting. Confirm that the details are correct and that you have followed the form’s instructions.

Applicants should not assume that completing the form guarantees selection. The supplied information does not describe the selection criteria, notification date, number of available places or whether applicants will be interviewed.

APPLY HERE

9. Application Deadline and Important Dates

The announcement specifies three dates on which participants must be available:

Date Requirement
14 November 2026 Required availability
1 December 2026 Required availability
2 December 2026 Required availability

Application deadline: The supplied announcement and form excerpt do not state a submission deadline.

Applicants should consult the official UNICEF Malaysia announcement or application form for any deadline or additional timeline information. Because the first required date is 14 November 2026, interested youth leaders should check the official application channel promptly rather than assume that applications will remain open indefinitely.

Click HERE for more information about UNICEF Malaysia Youth Call 2026.

10. Is Funding or Financial Support Provided?

The supplied announcement does not state whether participants will receive a stipend, transport allowance, accommodation, meals, reimbursement or other financial support.

It also does not specify whether the programme is free of charge or whether participants must cover their own travel and other costs.

Applicants should contact UNICEF Malaysia or consult the full official programme information to confirm:

  • Whether participation is free.
  • Whether travel costs are covered.
  • Whether meals or refreshments are provided.
  • Whether accommodation is available or funded if required.
  • Whether local transportation support is available.
  • Whether any additional costs are associated with participation.

Candidates should not make financial assumptions based solely on the supplied announcement.

11. Frequently Asked Questions

Who can apply for the UNICEF Malaysia environmental manifesto initiative?

The stated target group is youth leaders aged 15 to 24 who reside in Malaysia and can be present in the country and available on 14 November, 1 December and 2 December 2026.

Must applicants live in Malaysia?

Yes. The announcement specifically states that participants must be residing in Malaysia and must be in the country for the required dates.

Can applicants from outside Malaysia apply?

The call is directed at young people residing in Malaysia. The supplied material does not explicitly specify nationality requirements or confirm whether foreign citizens who live in Malaysia are eligible. Applicants who need clarification should contact UNICEF Malaysia.

What will participants do?

Participants will co-create a Manifesto for a Safe, Clean, Healthy and Sustainable Environment and present it to Members of Parliament.

Do applicants need previous environmental experience?

The supplied announcement does not specify previous environmental experience, a particular academic qualification or a minimum level of leadership experience as mandatory requirements.

Can applicants under 18 participate?

The form includes a question asking applicants under 18 whether they can obtain written parental or guardian consent if selected. Applicants in this age group should be prepared to meet this condition.

Is the opportunity specifically for Indigenous youth?

The form asks whether applicants identify as Indigenous, but the supplied information does not state that the opportunity is restricted to Indigenous applicants. It should not be interpreted as an Indigenous-only call without confirmation from UNICEF Malaysia.

Is there an application fee?

The supplied material does not state whether there is an application fee. Applicants should confirm this through the official application channel and avoid paying unofficial intermediaries.

What is the deadline?

No application deadline is visible in the supplied announcement and form excerpt. The programme requires availability on 14 November, 1 December and 2 December 2026, and applicants should check the official form for submission instructions and any deadline.

Where can applicants find the form?

The supplied excerpt does not contain the complete form URL. Applicants should access it through the official UNICEF Malaysia announcement or a verified UNICEF Malaysia communication.

Conclusion

The UNICEF Malaysia Manifesto for a Safe, Clean, Healthy and Sustainable Environment open call offers young people an opportunity to contribute to a collective environmental manifesto and present it to Members of Parliament. By seeking participants aged 15 to 24 who reside in Malaysia, the initiative places youth participation at the centre of a process focused on environmental priorities.

Interested applicants should first confirm that they meet the age and residence requirements and can attend all three required dates: 14 November, 1 December and 2 December 2026. They should also complete the application form carefully, provide accurate contact details, communicate any reasonable accommodation needs and prepare written parental or guardian consent if they are under 18 and selected.

The supplied announcement does not identify an application deadline, funding arrangements or the complete application URL. Prospective participants should verify these details through UNICEF Malaysia’s official channels before submitting their information. Eligible young people who are interested in environmental advocacy and contributing their perspectives to a manifesto for parliamentary representatives should review the full application instructions and apply through the verified official form.
